versions.changelog: Simplify the login instructions to the code flow (maton login prints a link; finish with maton login --code <CODE>), drop the API Key subsection, and pin the Maton CLI install to 0.4.0.
Switch the login instructions to the device flow (maton login prints a link and a user code; the --oauth flag is gone) and pin the Maton CLI install to 0.3.5.
Pin the Maton CLI install to 0.3.4, the current release.

Add this skill's own trigger policy to the shared Triggers section: the only destination it sets up is its own hosted function inside the platform, it does not forward events to third-party hosts, and it does not use event watch --exec; each trigger reference now also says this skill configures no trigger from that source on its own.

Bring the skill to the current api-gateway baseline and tell the connection-to-function-to-trigger story: the shared Functions and Triggers sections open with an example for this app (a hosted function that performs one action for it through the Maton SDK, and the trigger that runs it - its own event source where it has one, otherwise a time schedule), the description says these constructs turn the connection into automation and add no capability of their own, the passthrough is described by its enforced boundary, CLI and SDK installs are pinned to 0.3.1, absolute API URLs are placeholders, and multipart uploads use mktemp.
CLI-first rewrite with the Maton SDK examples; clarify that the CLI and SDKs keep separate credential stores, and reword webhook egress warnings

CLI-first rewrite: the maton CLI with OAuth login is the documented path, every example is a maton command, SDK examples added, and the raw HTTP fallback feeds the key on stdin instead of reading it from the environment

- Updated all API endpoints and connection management URLs from gateway.maton.ai and ctrl.maton.ai to api.maton.ai.
- Clarified that connection management endpoints are Maton platform operations, not part of the Make API.
- Removed the redundant skill-card.md file.
- No changes to API usage or functionality.

- Added a requirement that all write operations (create, update, start, stop, delete) require explicit user approval before execution.
- Updated documentation to clarify user confirmation is needed for all modifications, enhancing security and preventing unintended changes.
- No functional changes to API endpoints or integration flow.
- LICENSE.txt file removed.

- Added important warnings about persistent and destructive operations to the description and Security & Permissions section.
- Clarified that only listed API endpoints are supported.
- Updated connection header usage instructions; emphasized specifying the connection if multiple exist.
- Improved documentation on resource persistence and risk of affecting live workflows.
- Refined Security & Permissions with detailed guidance on organizational scope and confirmation before deletes/stops.

- General documentation improvements for clarity and consistency.
- Updated example placeholders to use `{connection_id}` instead of hardcoded IDs.
- Expanded and clarified code examples in the connection management section.
- No functional or structural changes to the skill.

Initial release — integrates Make (formerly Integromat) API with managed authentication.

- Manage scenarios, organizations, teams, connections, data stores, hooks, and templates via the Maton API gateway.
- Includes detailed setup, authentication, and usage instructions with environment variable support.
- Provides Python code samples for common operations (list/create/delete connections, specify connection, etc.).
- Supports all standard Make API endpoints with proxy handling and connection management.
- Useful for automating workflows and integrating apps through Make with secure credential management.
